newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed up at 43.05 to the dollar on Thursday in the kerb amid dollar profit-taking. Dealers said official denials of further devaluation might boost the rupee rise after the Friday holiday.
Finance Minister Naveed Qamar said the exchange rate would not be changed for the "foreseeable future". Dealers said this had halted a dollar buying spree and could send the rupee up.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar. The premium on forex bearer certificates closed at 7.30 percent, after Wednesday's 7.40 percent close. -- Ovais Subhani 9221-5685192
